1972 Chevrolet Nova Is Anything But Original, Rocks 'Big Shoes' and a Proper Stance For the LSA V8
12 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
The Chevrolet Chevy II, aka Chevy Nova , was originally a compact car produced between the 1962 and 1979 model years. It was the inaugural model for the then-new GM X platform, tucked between the Chevrolet Corvair and the beloved Chevelle in the brand’s model line.
From 1969 onward, all versions adopted the famous Chevrolet Nova moniker, and the nameplate went down in history especially because of the success of the third generation among automotive enthusiasts – rooted in the fact that Chevrolet quickly understood the potential of the Nova Super Sport turning from a simple trim option into a veritable performance package and into one of the smallest muscle cars from Detroit.
Nevertheless, the idea was quite popular and led to the arrival of other derivatives like the Rally Nova or the creation of the Yenko Novas by the retired race car driver and muscle car specialist Don Yenko of Yenko Chevrolet in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, who took the Nova alongside Chevelles and Camaros to modify for extra performance – turning them into weapons against the Ford Mustangs, Plymouth Barracudas and Dodge Challengers of the time.
The special Chevy was even known as the Yenko Supernova, and all these had tremendous impact on enthusiasts, who love the series even today – some more than others, and in many different ways. While many classic car aficionados love keeping them just the same as they were during the moment they went out of the factory gates, the restomod current has gained more and more traction in recent years – mixing the classic looks with modern performance and maneuverability.
This is the case here, as proudly announced by Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors : “If the stance and shoes aren't a big enough hint, this '72 Nova is anything but original. Another resto-modded classic muscle car graces our showroom and announced its arrival without subtlety.” The package includes a Nova sourced from a private collection and professionally built by GR Classics.
It’s finished in white over black with black Rally stripes, and this Chevy Nova has less than 2,500 miles recorded on the odometer since it was built. It comes with oversized Rally-style reproduction wheels, and under the hood resides a potent LS3 V8 packing 6.2 liters and an LSA supercharger, delivering both power and “an unforgettable exhaust note” through the Black Widow dual exhaust.
The V8 is paired with a 4L80 automatic transmission equipped with a B&M Slap Shifter; a Holley EFI system with a touchscreen interface provides modern engine management; the “chassis and braking system have been upgraded to match the car's impressive power,” and there’s even push-button start for the mighty V8.
Inside, the classic Chevy Nova cabin has a custom black bucket seat arrangement, a bespoke stereo system with Bluetooth connectivity, Vintage Air conditioning, and custom switchgear to go with the Kenwood audio and the Procar Rally Smoothback buckets. Of course, it ain’t cheap: the asking price is $94,900 – but at least it’s not a six-figure deal.

BMW's New X5 Gets a Mild Tuning Job in Fantasy Land
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
Unless you’ve been living under a rock these past few months, completely cut off from the car world, then you know that BMW has an entirely new X5 (among other things) in its lineup.
The fifth generation hit the assembly line in August at the Spartanburg factory in the United States of America, and it also has a long wheelbase sibling, the G78, which comes to life in China, at the Dadong facility in Shenyang, for the local market. The G65 is based on an updated version of the old model’s CLAR construction, so despite looking entirely new, it shares many traits with its predecessor, though you cannot see them at first glance.
If you are familiar with BMW’s Neue Klasse design language, then you know why the new-gen X5 looks the way it does. And here, we are talking about the design of the kidney grille, which some say is a joke, whereas others definitely like. The same goes for the new X-shaped headlights, and the aggressive design of the front bumper, with its large air intake in the middle, separated in half by a pair of vertical slats, and the vents flanking it on the outer edges, and on the outer parts of the bumper.
Did you think that the profile is not controversial at all? In that case, you clearly haven’t heard that instead of traditional door handles, or even flush-mounted ones, the new-gen BMW X5 has some winglets. As a result, the doors look cleaner overall, at least on the upper sections, because the lower parts are on the sharp-looking side of things, just like the side skirts. And for whatever reason, BMW decided to add some angular-styled lines around the wheel arches.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik The back end design is also Neue Klasse , with its new taillight signature, aggressive rear bumper, and different tailgate, which, by the way, has lost its split-opening party trick. And the cockpit is also controversial due to the addition of the Panoramic iDrive. That’s the display that stretches from one pillar to the other at the bottom of the windshield. And it’s joined by a free-floating infotainment screen, and an optional passenger display, as well as a four-spoke steering wheel.
Given that the all-new BMW X5 is not exactly a looker anymore, at least in some people’s eyes, and when compared to the older generations, we have seen quite a few rendering takes on it that try to make it a bit more appealing. The latest to have crossed our screens came from @kelsonik on Instagram, and they imagine the new premium mid-size crossover with some headlight tweaks, as well as new wheels, and a few other modifications.
Mind you, while the headlights of this rendered G65 retain their size and shape, they feature yellow daytime running lights for a more aggressive stance. The trim on the grille is now black, and black is the color that was virtually applied to the car’s entire exterior. And since this color tends to hide quirky looks very nicely, as everyone knows, the end product is definitely a lot more appealing. That’s what I think, anyway.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Before inviting you to contradict me in the comments box below, I also have to mention other virtual modifications, because the rendered BMW X5 has also been imagined with two different sets of wheels. Both have a multi-spoke design, albeit with different patterns, but one is a lot more concave than the other. Both alloy sets sport a black finish, and in one case, they brake calipers are red, whereas in the other, they’re black.
Before wrapping it up, the pixel artist has also adjusted the suspension using the same photo-editing software, so this CGI-infused new-gen BMW X5 now sits a bit closer to the ground. The front and rear bumpers, side skirts, door mirrors, roof-mounted spoiler, and everything else carry over from the real thing.
As you likely know, the Neue Klasse BMW X5 starts from $69,800 in the United States of America. This is the MSRP of the X5 40, which is the base version of the crossover. The 40 xDrive variant kicks off at $72,100, and both feature the same 3.0-liter TwinPower Turbo inline-six engine, which develops 394 hp (400 ps/294 kW). The RWD model needs 5.2 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and the AWD one completes the sprint in 5.1 seconds.
BMW also offers the X5 50E xDrive plug-in hybrid, which combines the same inline-six with an electric motor for a total output of 483 hp (490 ps/360 kW). That’s the same as its direct predecessor, and the same goes for the 0-60 mph, which takes 4.6 seconds. However, instead of 39 miles (63 km), it can now travel up to 44 miles (71 km) on electric power alone. Pricing starts at $77,500 in this case.

Once Revolutionary, this 20-Year-Old American Yacht Is Now Asking for $20M
28 photos
Photo: Denison Yachting
Is it really worth spending nearly $20 million on a yacht below 50 meters that’s been around for two decades? Beyond what industry experts have to say, the answer is highly subjective. No matter what, the 2006 Christensen that made an appearance at this year’s Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show hides a trailblazing origin making it much more exciting that what can be seen superficially.
When someone today is looking at a decades-old yacht, it’s hard for them to imagine and to feel the enthusiasm and sheer excitement of what that yacht represented 20 years ago, when it was officially presented to the world. Today, Crili might seem like just another yacht below 50 meters from Christensen, but the truth is that Crili was a true pioneer at the time of its launch.
To be able to fully appreciate what this American yacht means today, we must take a short trip down memory lane and try to picture it as the fresh Christensen delivery that everyone in the industry was talking about in 2006. Launched as Hull 028, Barchetta was the newest in an already successful series of tri-deck 157-footers (48 meters). It was similar to its predecessors, but also very different.
Exactly twenty years ago, in November 2006, Mike Smith was writing in Power &Motoryacht about the powerful debut of the intriguing new Christensen. The shipyard’s strategy as the time was to deliver three yachts per year, which meant they were starting to build a new boat in the 157-foot series every three months.
Photo: Denison Yachting It was the magic of semi-custom yachts – perfect for the busy owners who wanted the freedom to personalize their luxury boats, but without the waiting time associated with a custom yacht. Most of the work on Barchetta was done in-house, except for the interior design, officially handled by Jacqueline Mann Design, but with major input from the owner who, according to Dudley Dawson, who reviewed this yacht in the Yachting Magazine a year later, in 2027, was “a lady”.
While building on the earlier successful deliveries in that same series, Barchetta took on a trailblazing role that would make it unique. First, it became the first-ever Christensen yacht to sport a bulbous bow, specifically for improved fuel efficiency and better range. To achieve this, Christensen worked with the prestigious New York-based Webb Institute, and planned to apply this innovation to all future yachts in the series.
Boasting a massive maximum displacement of 800,000 lbs, Barchetta was also the heaviest Christensen at the time (explained, according to Mike Smith, by the use of 0.75-inch stone slab for all the interior). Yet, what made it remarkable was the proven 17-knot top speed, even at this weight. This performance was apparently also possible thanks to the innovative bulbous bow.
Beyond the engineering upgrades, Barchetta flaunted what everyone at the time agreed was a spectacular Art Deco interior. Maximalist, bold, and openly flamboyant, the owner-curated original interior design featured dramatic elements like black resin inlays inspired by the Chrysler Building, custom glass artwork in the owner’s en-suite, and striking decorative accents in hot red (including the leather upholstery and bed linens).
Photo: Denison Yachting This pure shade of red became a signature symbol for the yacht, beyond the purely decorative accents – from the nameplate that looked stunning against the classic white hull backdrop to the engines themselves, a pair of large MTUs. Another statement feature was the original owner’s personal art collection of expensive crystal and glass pieces, including Lalique.
In fact, as Dudley Dawson vividly describes, it looked as if Barchetta’s interior design in neutral tones and contrasting black inlays was meant to become the perfect canvas for the owner’s Art Deco collection. This is even more unusual considering that the 2006 Christensen was intended for charter operations from the start.
Apparently, the owner made sure to set up specific security measures for all the artwork throughout, as well as protecting it against any kind of damage, and even the precious upholstery was specifically treated to be water-resistant, for the same reason.
As it inevitably happens, the 2006 yacht that was the largest Christensen at the time and the first one to sport a bulbous bow, changed ownership several times, and its original sparkle faded more with each new change of hands.
Photo: Denison Yachting Reportedly, Crili’s most recent owner was a Florida-based billionaire, the late Alfonso Fanjul, one of the two billionaire brothers associated with a sugar empire. Forbes called them “The Florida Sugar Barons” with Cuban roots and an important presence in Florida. Alfonso Fanjul passed away earlier this year, and perhaps that explains why Crili joined the market and attended FLIBS just a few months later.
This year, when it was featured at FLIBS twenty years after its launch, the renamed Crili was no longer one of the most impressive and innovative American yachts around.
Still, it’s just as coveted as brand-new yacht in the same size category, mainly thanks to the continuous upkeep and recent upgrades. A full paint job, the rebuild of its main engines and transmissions, plus a professional engine room repaint are some of the highlights completed in 2023, 2025, and 2026.
In 2025, Crili has also completed its mandatory 20-year class survey, a confirmation of its ABS classification that allows it, among other things, to activate as a charter yacht. Considering all the upgrades completed over the years, plus the yacht’s original Christensen DNA and proven charter history, the $19.7 million price tag seems justified, even for a yacht this age and below the unofficial superyacht size threshold.
Photo: Denison Yachting Boasting interior volume just under 500 GT, Crili can easily accommodate at least 14 guests, and even more. The classic configuration features a full-beam, main-deck owner’s suite, and five more guest suites. Since the beginning, dedicated quarters for a generous ten-person crew were also more spacious and better equipped than the standard at the time.
Beautiful amenities onboard include an elegant formal dinner reminiscent of the yacht’s original Art Deco aesthetic, a fully-equipped gym, a light-filled main salon showcasing the original glossy wood paneling throughout, and a large jacuzzi, plus grill facilities, on the sun deck.
As soon it had dived into charter operations, Crili packed a hefty toybox, even an exciting mini submarine for three. Today, jet skis, inflatable water toys, and larger tenders are available for charter guests. Just as important, Crili has the fuel storage capacity to support extended cruising without too many stops. A perfect vacation yacht in every way, Crili combines the comfort of a floating mansion with the proven track record of charter success.
Although, unfortunately, few people today remember what this beautiful 2006 Christensen meant at the time and how dazzling it was in its original era, Crili remains one of the most important yachts in the American shipyard’s history, and an excellent US-built pleasure craft overall.
Photo: Denison Yachting The American shipyard that started building composite luxury yachts in Vancouver, Washington, in the late 1990s, delivered yachts that are still famous today, such as John Staluppi’s Casino Royale and Tiger Woods’ Privacy. Crili didn’t make headlines like some of these better-known Christensens, but it’s just as remarkable, and won’t most likely need to wait too long for its next owner, even with that intimidating $19.7 million price tag.

Beautiful Tiny House Pours French Sparkle Over Self-Sufficient Living
26 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
“Open Air” is a beautiful and wonderfully fitting name for a tiny house on wheels designed to turn the joy of being outdoors into a way of living. Equipped for a comfortable off-grid lifestyle, tiny house Plein Air adds that lovely French touch that makes even the humblest mobile abode seem like a piece of fairytale.
A wood-burning fireplace, mysterious timber shutters at all the windows, and the aroma of natural wood, inside and out – this is, in a nutshell, the formula of an enchanting homely ambiance. The builder of tiny house Plein Air, Mon Reve en Bois, describes it poetically as “happiness all year round”, and what could be better than that? This perfect, wholesome happiness comes from reliable autonomy, enhanced comfort, and harmony with nature.
Tiny house Plein Air is French in every way, yet it offers beautiful volume throughout, and one of the best layouts by all standards, simply thanks to a bigger size. Legally, this spacious home is still designed as a tiny house approved for the road, but everything about it was thought out for long-term accommodation, settled somewhere in a beautiful environment. The builder presents it as one of their best models for couples and even family living.
This generous volume, carefully organized into one of the most efficient layouts, comes from a length of 8.5 meters (27.8 feet), a 3-meter (9.8 feet) width, and an exterior height of slightly over four meters (13 feet). In total, Tiny Plein Air offers 34.5 square meters (372 square feet) of floor space, considerably more than the average French tiny house.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Although the single loft in this configuration is the only formal bedroom, Tiny Plein Air can accommodate up to four people thanks to a lovely, big lounge that can double as a second room. It also boasts a charming L-shaped kitchen that takes up one end of the house, and a fully-equipped bathroom (nestled right next to the kitchen).
This configuration sounds basic, yet the added spaciousness for each living space inside this tiny house allows for greater versatility which, in turn, improves functionality beyond what is typically attainable in a regular 6-meter home on wheels built in France. For instance, the open lounge can be much more than a simple space for relaxation. A pop-up tabletop, made of pure timber, turns this area into a dining room.
Looking almost invisible when folded, this pop-up table located near the main entrance, makes room for at least four seats. Plus, additional tables and chairs can make their way closer to the sofa, allowing for even more dining options. Resting against the wall, the lounge sofa combines comfy seating with built-in storage. The free floor space in this part of the house is like an open invitation for a workspace, hobbies, yoga, and many more.
A lot more is possible thanks to the residential-style separation between the lounge and the kitchen. In compact homes on wheels, these two areas are often intertwined. Tiny Plein Air, however, places each one at a separate end, which allows full functionality and also frees up a large section of floor space in the transition area between them. When it comes to tiny living, every extra inch of free floor space equals luxury.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Large windows help make this spacious tiny house seem even bigger by flooding it with natural light. Two windows in the lounge, two windows in the kitchen area, and two windows in the loft bedroom – there’s no scarcity when it comes to natural light and fresh air (the bathroom, of course, has its own window as well).
The L-shaped kitchen is one of the most unique features of Tiny Plein Air. Its placement is unusual (most of the times, kitchens are found in the center, with the lounge at one end and the bathroom at the other end), and the L-shaped design translates to a more generous counter surface and better storage compared to the usual compact kitchens. Those who appreciate the quality of natural timber will also love the beautiful bespoke cabinetry.
There are no upper cupboards at all, which results in a brighter and airier cooking space, especially with those two large windows bringing in extra light. Bespoke cabinets offer sufficient storage, including separate nooks for appliances.
Additional storage is available in the staircase located between the bathroom and the lounge. Custom-crafted like the rest of the furniture, it turns only a few treads into hidden drawers, and also features a larger cabinet built into it. It’s not the crazy built-in storage you see in other staircases, with tens of drawers and cabinets throughout, but it enhances the home’s storage capacity in an elegant, more discrete way, that doesn’t clash with the airy interior.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The staircase leads to a deliciously spacious loft bedroom, far better than what many French tiny homes offer. Even with a standard double bed, there’s ample walk-around space. Built-in cabinets at the head of the bed match the minimalist nightstands. Large windows on each side keep the air circulating while adding the luxury of glorious views.
The version of Tiny Plein Air pictured in the gallery comes with a complete off-grid kit, including everything from solar power to water tanks, and water filtration systems. The wood-burning fireplace sitting in a dedicated, insulated corner of the lounge is not just for fun – it’s actually the only source of heat for this self-sufficient abode. The same goes for the toilet, which may look rustic, but is in fact a waterless design meant to save water and energy.
Like all the models from this French builder based in Occitania, Tiny Plein Air is a living tribute to the beauty of raw timber, inside and out. This builder prides itself in only using certified timber obtained from sustainably-managed local woods in Occitania – a practice that supports local craftsmanship and this priceless natural resource.
Self-sufficient, but not rugged to the point where it feels uninviting – this French tiny house knows how to sprinkle the special magic that makes any plain house feel like home. The traditional aesthetic that might seem too rustic for some is, in fact, what minimalism in harmony with nature should look like. There’s absolutely nothing artificial, cheap, or cookie-cutter about this lovely interior, and this actually makes it more luxurious than an expensive mansion.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois This is the kind of luxury that isn’t reflected in the price tag. The fully-equipped version pictured in the gallery, complete with a full autonomy kit, is valued at under €70,000 ($77,000). The only downside is that French tiny homes are available exclusively in France. As small companies and artisan workshops, most tiny house builders in this country deliver only locally or throughout France, at best.
Still, such a beautiful tiny house like Plein Air, from its perfect layout to the craftsmanship quality, can become a rich source of inspiration for anyone in search of their dream tiny homes. The world of tiny house design is much more versatile than many people think, from the most traditional perspective to radical contemporary style.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Tiny house Plein Air is proof that you don’t necessarily need an XL tiny house for comfortable tiny living, and also that an all-wood home on wheels can be just as cozy and functional as its more modern counterparts.

2027 Volkswagen T-Roc R Performance Crossover Gets Teased With Series-Production Everything
17 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The largest European automaker of them all has recently published official spy photos of the upcoming T-Roc R, showcasing a prototype loaded with series-production body panels and trim pieces. Its rear end tells us quite a bit about the direction of this crossover, starting with the quad exhaust outlets and sporty-looking aerodynamic diffuser.
Equipped with front and rear light bars connecting the headlight and taillight clusters, the 2027 model further prides itself on illuminated VW badging. Performance-oriented wheels and larger brakes can also be seen, whereas the front bumper gets its own aggressive treatment, separating the performance version from lesser T-Roc trim levels.
Disguised under blue-and-white camo wrap, the next-generation Volkswagen T-Roc R also benefits from larger front bumper openings. Not only does it have different cooling requirements due to its 2.0-liter turbo iron-block gasoline mill, but a performance-oriented crossover also has to cool its front brakes properly.
Its four tailpipes are particularly interesting, with Volkswagen using quad pipes to distinguish full-on R models from the regular trim level range. Circular tips are on the menu, and there is a slim chance that Volkswagen will offer an optional Akrapovic performance exhaust setup. In the previous generation's case, the Akrapovic unit was manufactured exclusively from high-grade titanium alloy.
Lighter than the stock stainless-steel system, the Akrapovic exhaust also makes sense when you remember that its compact hatchback and wagon siblings can also be had with titanium systems. The axle-back exhaust of the Golf R sheds roughly 7 kilograms (15 pounds) compared to the stainless-steel arrangement.
Photo: Volkswagen A different muffler also makes it stand out in the crowd. Titanium has different acoustic properties compared to stainless steel, and the resulting thinner walls resonate differently as well, giving the exhaust a crisper and higher-pitched edge under load. Slightly louder overrun crackles are part of its appeal as well.
Rolling on 20-inch forged alloys, the pictured test vehicle builds on the T-Roc R-Line's styling with more pronounced elements up front and for the rear end. As per Volkswagen's technical documentation for the second-generation T-Roc, a high-output 2.0 TSI with mild-hybrid assistance is planned for the compact-sized crossover, and the only application we can think of is the new T-Roc R.
In eTSI flavor, it's easy to imagine over 300 horsepower and more than 300 pound-feet of twist on premium unleaded. It remains to be seen, however, if the Wolfsburg-based manufacturer's R division will match or exceed the current Golf R's 328 horsepower and 310 pound-feet (420 Newton-meters). Neither the hatchback nor the wagon comes with a 48-volt system as of this writing.
Certain to feature the seven-speed DSG with wet clutches, the T-Roc R is a genuinely interesting thriller when you remember that Volkswagen is certain to use 4MOTION with R Performance Torque Vectoring. That's another way of saying two independently controlled multi-plate clutches for the rear axle. Similar to standard 4MOTION, this system also distributes up to 50 percent of the available torque to the rear wheels.
R Performance Torque Vectoring indicates that all of the torque going to the rear axle can be sent to either rear wheel, helping the T-Roc R rotate better while cornering to reduce understeer, thus helping the driver accelerate out of the corner faster. R Performance Torque Vectoring also features a Drift Mode on the Golf R, and this mode is certain to carry over to the T-Roc R as well.
According to Volkswagen's November 2025 fact sheet about the second-generation T-Roc , the R will be unleashed at the beginning of 2027. With a bit of luck, the first units will be delivered in the summer of 2027. The FDA has denied an approval for Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab to treat EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, blocking the drug’s entry to the U.S. after it became available in China in 2024.
Ivonescimab, the PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody brought over to the U.S. from China by Summit Therapeutics, has been denied approval by the FDA for a certain type of lung cancer.
Summit had been seeking approval for ivonescimab in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after treatment with a TKI inhibitor. Had Summit earned the FDA nod, it would have marked the first approval for a PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody in the U.S. market. The drug has been available in China through partner Akeso since 2024 for this indication.
The FDA issued a complete response letter (CRL) for Summit’s biologics license application (BLA), on the grounds that the application cannot be approved in its present form. The agency argued that the company has not established evidence of effectiveness because the therapy did not show a statistically significant overall survival (OS) benefit. The FDA said the drug’s progression-free survival benefit “in the absence of a statistically significant OS benefit” does not indicate a positive benefit-risk profile.
“We are disappointed for patients and their families awaiting additional treatment options in this setting,” said Robert Duggan, Co-CEO of Summit, in a Sunday statement. “We chose to pursue an ivonescimab regimen here based on the opportunity to provide another treatment option to help patients in need. In doing so, we believe the global HARMONi study provided the basis for a treatment option that these patients needed.”
Summit submitted the application to the FDA with evidence from the Phase 3 HARMONi trial, which showed improved progression-free survival with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy as compared to placebo. The trial for the first time replicated evidence seen in China and suggested Western patients could benefit to the same degree.
But the data were mixed, with ivonescimab missing on the OS endpoint. In September, Summit was able to present additional data to the FDA showing a slight benefit on OS in the overall global population, and analysts had been bullish that ivonescimab would go on to receive approval.
But it was not enough to woo the FDA. Summit pledged to continue developing the base of evidence for the therapy in multiple indications, including several types of NSCLC. The company did not, however, provide next steps for the EGFR indication in its Sunday release.
Companies have rushed to partner with Summit, with analysts heralding the drug as “the next major backbone” of cancer treatment, Graig Suvannavejh, managing director and senior biotech and biopharma analyst at Mizuho Securities, told BioSpace earlier this month .

EICMA 2026 • Honda Africa Twin Gets Biggest Refresh in a Decade, They Now Call It CRF1150L
Debrecen Plant Starts 2027 BMW iX4 Production in Hungary
22 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW's Hungarian vehicle plant has recently started production of the second Neue Klasse model assembled in Debrecen. iX4 is what the Bavarian automaker calls the coupe-ified sport utility vehicle, and its name alone is enough to understand that it's closely related to the more SUV-like iX3.
Its introduction followed a very quick production ramp-up for the iX3, with BMW Group Plant Debrecen introducing round-the-clock manufacturing in September 2026 due to rising demand for the less expensive battery-electric model. In the first instance, iX4 customers will be presented with the 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive variants of the zero-emission sport utility vehicle.
To be launched in Europe this coming spring, the iX4 will also be offered in M Performance flavor. The upcoming M60 xDrive should drop next year as well, packing more than 600 horsepower and precisely 645 pound-feet (875 Newton-meters) of twist in optimal conditions.
BMW Group Plant Debrecen reached a very important milestone back in July 2026 with the 50,000th unit of the iX3, the factory accomplishing this in less than a year. The German automaker reported more than 100,000 customer orders from European markets alone, hence the introduction of the third shift in September 2026.
More than 2 billion euros were invested by the company in the Debrecen complex, which occupies just around 400 hectares (988 acres) and targets 150,000 vehicles per annum. Building on the iX3, the iX4 distinguishes itself from the B-pillars back, flaunting a sloping roofline and a more dynamic rear end, liftgate and all. In 50 xDrive flavor, it promises up to 828 kilometers (514 miles) of WLTP range.
Photo: BMW That's marginally better than the iX3 50 xDrive, with both models benefiting from sixth-generation eDrive technology that includes cylindrical battery cells instead of the old prismatic design. Those in the market for the iX4 50 xDrive are presented with a very respectable 463 horsepower and 645 Newton-meters (476 pound-feet), along with 108.7 kilowatt-hours of high-voltage battery capacity.
Its dual-motor setup enables a 0-100 sprint of 4.9 seconds, which is approximately 4.7 seconds from zero to 60 miles per hour. Like its brother, the iX4 is much obliged to support 400-kW fast charging on direct current, making it a tremendously good electric vehicle for long-distance driving.
A 10-minute charging session can replenish up to 387 kilometers (240 miles) of WLTP range, but even in less-than-optimal conditions, the fast-charging system ensures that its battery will be sufficiently replenished in the time needed to enjoy a cup of coffee and a snack. Downgrading to the iX4 40 xDrive means 369 horsepower and 384 pound-feet (520 Newton-meters) of torque.
Its driving range and maximum DC charging capability slot below the 50 as well, with BMW quoting 638 kilometers (396 miles) and 300 kilowatts at most. At the other end of the spectrum, the M60 is a dual-motor affair that tops 777 kilometers (483 miles) on a full charge. Debrecen handles high-voltage battery assembly for all three, alongside stamping, painting, and final assembly.
The front and rear motors for both launch versions, however, come from Austria. BMW's Steyr plant is tasked with producing said motors, which are shared with the more affordable iX3 40 xDrive and iX3 50 xDrive.

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks .
Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.
“High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”
That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the company won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Eacon conducts the ORCASTRA
Screencap; via EACON.
SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors , adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the big bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.
“Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”
The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.
Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines , including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.
SANY SKT105ED
SANY delivered 200 haul trucks in August.
While specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the company has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain , pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.
Those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The big trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
This Mobile Home Is the First-Ever to Feature a Quad Loft, and It's a Winner
19 photos
Photo: The RV Hunter
No one ever invented an industry first just for bragging rights, though they too must come in handy every once in a while. Kropf Park RVs, an industry leading manufacturer of park tiny houses and prefabs, has just unveiled the industry's first-ever quad-loft mobile house.
Called the Island 6478QP, it's part of the Island series of park tinies, which Kropf describes as "customized comfort." They're the most budget-friendly floorplans Kropf offers in basic spec, but each can be customized to an insane degree, until it becomes as fancy – and as expensive – as the premium options in the catalog.
For 2027, Kropf is unveiling an Island that boasts an industry-first quad-loft, allowing it to offer maximum sleeping capacity of ten people – eight of whom will be crashing upstairs, in a giant loft that nonetheless offers some privacy as well. Far from feeling like a can of sardines on a quad-axle and home-like design, this park tiny is actually good-looking and surprisingly spacious.
Built on a heavy-duty custom trailer with four axles, this Island home comes in at 43 feet (13.1 meters) of total length and 12 feet (3.6 meters) of width. It's a park tiny certified as a Park RV, which means it's designed to stay put on location and only travel by special towing rig and with special towing permits.
Photo: The RV Hunter It's a mobile house in the strictest sense, but mobility is limited because of its widebody design. In return, it offers more space inside, truly residential features and appliances, and thanks to that quad-loft, a very high sleeping capacity.
The quad-loft is the cherry on this park house-shaped cake: the first loft in the industry to run the entire length of the home, from tip to front end. Hunter from The RV Hunter says in the video tour below that Kropf is looking to patent the construction method of that loft, which would make sense.
The best part about this extended loft is that it does more than just offer space for four full mattresses, and actually creates a sense of privacy, to the point where you can talk about four bedroom spaces upstairs. It does that by inserting a larger piece of furniture between each pair of mattresses, thus offering sleeping and storage for all the people using these spaces, and one window in each space.
Photo: The RV Hunter The first space is also the larger one and could be equipped with a kiddie playroom space, in case of families looking to turn the entire upstairs into the children's space.
Meanwhile, the grown-ups will be downstairs, and Kropf doesn't disappoint here. Entrance is done directly into the living room space, equipped with a pull-out sleeper sofa and couch and an entertainment wall with a large-screen TV.
The open-plan kitchen takes up the front of the trailer, with a large U-shaped cooking block that integrates a peninsula that doubles as a four-person dining area, a separate walk-in pantry with a coffee hutch, and a massive double-door fridge and freezer tucked under the loft, next to the sofa. If you're counting novelties with this floorplan, the walk-in pantry is also a first for an Island model, and an excellent addition for a floorplan that caters to such a large party.
Photo: The RV Hunter Finishes include dovetail joinery on the full-extension drawers, thermafoil counters (upgradable to solid surface), soft-close hinges, adjustable shelves on all the upper cabinets, real tile backsplashes, and only residential appliances. Even in a floorplan that prioritizes sleeping space, Kropf delivers the best, so you get a four-burner cooktop with a large griddle section, a large oven, and a full-size microwave.
The main bedroom is at the opposite end of the trailer, offered standard with a king bed with overhead cabinets and smaller overhead cubbies. At the foot of the bed is a full wardrobe with a chest of drawers, prep for a second TV, and lots of natural light coming in through the window you won't block if you choose not to have that TV.
The bedroom gets light through windows on three sides, but you also have the option to have the entire rear wall of glass, by adding sliding doors and maybe an optional porch.
Photo: The RV Hunter The only bathroom available is located across from the solid staircase to the loft. It's more on the compact side, but it still offers a plumbed toilet, a nice fiberglass shower with gliding glass doors, and a porcelain sink on a vanity with integrated storage. Knowing it would have to service up to 10 people, Kropf does its best to add extra storage, including a linen closet and a smaller medicine cabinet over the toilet.
The unit shown below is more or less standard, so while it's nice to look at, it's not the nicest looking you can get from Kropf.
Photo: The RV Hunter That's the biggest selling point of an Island park home, according to the manufacturer : "an impressive list of standard features with endless upgrade possibilities to make sure your park model has all the comforts you desire without paying for any you don't."
This will come at a price, obviously. There's no MSRP or sale price mentioned for the display unit below, but I came across a slightly different 6478QP with a sale price of $136,845.

Billy Is a Dog-Friendly Fiat Ducato Camper Van Made for Easygoing Adventures
19 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions
Meet Billy, a mobile home based on an L4H3 Fiat Ducato Maxi. It's the latest project made by Vanlife Conversions, an Essex, UK-based company that, as its name suggests, specializes in camper van conversions.
Billy was built for clients who love traveling and bringing their dogs along for the adventure. You'll definitely see that reflected in the interior design. Before we peek inside, let's see what the van sports on the outside.
You can tell straight away when laying eyes on the van that it's meant for adventuring. For starters, the vehicle rides on black Rogue Alloy wheels wrapped in General Grabber all-terrain tires.
Beyond the wheel and tire combo, another element reveals the fact that the van is meant to go off the beaten path. The lower part of the van was coated in Raptor truck bed liner to provide extra protection against stone chips and scratches.
At the rear, you'll come across a swing-away Thule bike rack for two bikes, attached to the hitch receiver.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions Other notable mods are power and water hookups, a small powered step by the sliding door, a 540 W solar array, and a Thule Omnistor awning.
Enter, and a roomy, beautifully designed interior will welcome you. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a large curtain to separate the two areas for more privacy and better insulation. Above it, you'll come across a large headliner compartment.
The passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van. Even better, you can use it as part of a simple seating area, as you can attach a Lagun table to a mount on the B-pillar by the entrance.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for white laminated cabinetry, white walls, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, and a slatted wood ceiling. The look is complemented by bright orange elements, like the curtain and couch cushion upholstery, and a blue subway tile backsplash.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions Dead ahead as you step inside, Vanlife Conversions added a bathroom behind a tall standard door. It boasts a shower with a mixer and a handheld wand, a wall niche for shampoos and soaps, and a removable Nature's Head composting toilet. I love its look, with white subway tile walls and a teak shower mat.
Next, we have the kitchen on the driver's side. It features a 100-liter Indel B fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, a single-burner induction stovetop, and a deep sink with a pull-out faucet. Three overhead cabinets, three drawers, and two lower cabinets are available for storage.
A simple but comfy seating area sits opposite the kitchen. It has two benches facing one another with a Lagun swivel table in the middle. The best part about this area is that it can be transformed into a small bed – you just have to use the table to connect the benches, and then rearrange the cushions.
The rear part of the living space offers the perfect setup for relaxing or sleeping after a long day in nature. You'll discover a bed arranged east to west that measures 190 centimeters (74 inches) in length.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions The bedroom also features three overhead cabinets and two reading lights. A nice touch is that you can leave the rear doors open for a breeze of fresh air, but you can close two curtains to have some privacy.
Alternatively, you can open two small windows integrated into the rear doors, and turn on the ceiling Maxxair vent fan above the bed to create a draft. The latter can be set up to either extract air out or blow air in.
Finally, the part of the van underneath the bedroom was turned into the garage. It offers a bit of storage space and accommodates part of the utility systems in two boxes on the sides. Moreover, it doubles as a bedroom for the dogs, as it has a dog crate that's accessible from the living space through a pass-through.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 460 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources allow you to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging via the alternator while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions As for plumbing, the van is equipped with an 83-liter (22-gallon) freshwater tank, an under-mounted 62-liter (16-gallon) greywater tank, an outdoor shower connection, and a reverse osmosis water filter.
The builders made one more dog-related modification to the van. They added hooks outside the van, bolted to the vehicle's underside, which allow you to tie a long leash for the dog.
All in all, Billy by Vanlife Conversions shows us just how practical a small space can become provided you use the right design. I'm sure both the customer and their furry friend will make lots of amazing memories in this camper van.

No, we don’t need a dose of antivenom – not if we’re bitten by something like this, because we’ll embrace its insanity with open minds and hearts. Anyway, the story of the Dodge Viper began as a crazy bet that no one except Bob Lutz thought it could be won. Back then, Chrysler’s president of operations had an idea in 1988: what if their company produced a true American sports car, but following the guidelines of the original Shelby Cobra?
Basically, Lutz thought it was a good idea to make a Chrysler model with crazy looks, raw and unabated power, plus great performance. Of course, as it turned out, the result was even more than the corner office head honcho had dreamt, although we have to say that his daringness to take a V10 engine that was being developed for the heavy-duty Dodge Ram pickup truck series and fit it into a sports car was pretty bonkers by any standards.
They also used suspension parts from the smaller Dakota model – which was also a pickup truck. We know, we know, it sounds like they were high on something, but it wasn’t just Lutz, as lead truck engineer François Castaing and Chrysler designer Tom Gale also fell in love with the project. Insanity was a common trait, it seems, as these were the roaring 1980s. Carroll Shelby himself later went with the Cobra-inspired Chrysler to the company’s CEO Lee Iacocca in support of his fellow comrades.
Photo: Motorcar Classics Upon approval, the concept was quickly brought to life – probably out of fear of the big kahunas sobering up and sending their ideas to the junk station. A concept car was ready within months, and the Viper was even brought to life on a very ‘small’ budget for an automaker like Chrysler, around $80 million. Naturally, with its looks and the sum of its parts, it was a flawed car, but the striking premise caused a massive sensation, and the Viper became a legend.
It was also a big contrast between the brawny looks and the number of people that were able to tame it, so early in the production years it was considered a massively intimidating car to drive, as there was massive power and torque but limited driver assistance from electronic nannies. That’s something almost inconceivable now, right?
Anyway, its legend only grew through the years, and Chrysler plus its later installments kept the Dodge Viper until 2017 and across five generations with a single small hiatus for the final installment. The fourth generation – ZB II – came out in 2008 and brought with it a new 8.4-liter V10 packing 600 horsepower and a massive 560 lb-ft of torque (759 Nm). This 2008 Dodge Viper SRT-10 Roadster is, of course, of the ZB II variety, and Farmingdale, New York-based Motorcar Classics “is proud to present this exceptional specimen of raw American muscle.”
Photo: Motorcar Classics This 2008 Dodge Viper SRT-10 has just 5,548 original miles, as it was in the care of a single owner all this time, and a clean CARFAX report, along with “an ideal history emerging from a prominent private collection.” Besides the fact that a design like the Viper won’t ever go unnoticed, the car is also dressed in a neck-snapping Viper Snakeskin Green Pearlcoat paint with white racing stripes and a black soft top, along with a classic black leather interior.
Of course, the dealership knows “this fourth-generation (ZB II) Viper represents a high point in American performance engineering, powered by a massive, naturally aspirated 8.4-liter V10 engine co-developed with McLaren Performance Technologies.” Its 600 hp and 560 lb-ft of torque channeled through a precise Tremec TR-6060 six-speed manual transmission are still worthy of our attention even today in the age of boring or plain ugly-looking EV hypercars boasting over 1,000 horsepower but also no soul whatsoever.
Photo: Motorcar Classics A representative of an age long gone, the “analogue beast rockets from 0 to 60 mph in under 3.5 seconds and commands a top speed exceeding 200 mph,” continues the description. They continue: “Beyond its overwhelming performance, this 2008 Viper holds immense historical and collectability significance. It stands as the quintessential expression of the traditional driver's supercar—offering pure, unadulterated mechanical engagement without electronic traction controls or driver aids to dilute the experience.”
The color is also sublime, and the ultra-low-mileage survivor is seen more like an “investment-grade opportunity for the discerning enthusiast or serious collector” than a thrill car for a true enthusiast. Of course, maybe it’s also the price that gets in the way, as the company asks $124,900 but leaves the door open for negotiations via the ‘make an offer’ button on their online listing. Cool or not?

COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC says every system worked normally.
It wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.
The CE-25A: 19 seats, 10 fans, 400 km
The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.
The CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.
The CATL connection
The obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL launched its aviation unit .
CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and said it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither company has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.
~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.
How it compares
COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, New York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.
Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.
Heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022 , and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery . Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.
Electrek’s Take
For years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.
Look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September , and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.
Now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.
And this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.
China also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

Self-Driving Luxury Trailer Pebble Flow Is Faulty, Falling Apart After One Year, Owners Say
87 photos
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing
This could be a case of a bad apple in a good batch or a cautionary tale. Ryan and Celeste, owners of one of the first units of the Pebble Flow produced, are going on the record with their nightmarish first year of ownership and how their unit is falling apart under their very eyes.
Pebble Flow is described by California-based startup Pebble RV as the travel trailer of the future. It's smart in every way imaginable, from the way it parks, hitches, or drives itself, to the way it dumps the black tank or obscures its windows when you want privacy. It's fully electric and with a clean, minimalist design that still makes room for a family of four.
Pebble Flow is, above everything else, a premium product with a price tag to match. Designed for digital nomads or travelers for whom being pioneers weighs heavily in a purchase decision, it starts at around $113,000 before options for the most basic spec.
It will start at that price, better said. Right now, Pebble is delivering the Founders Edition units, which come at prices around $175,000, with volume production scheduled to start once these deliveries wrap.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing Ryan and Celeste got a Founders Edition Pebble in November 2025, a 2026 unit they paid $190,000. As such, it came with all the bells and whistles that Pebble offers, as well as the "privilege" of being one of the first owners of such a trailer in the U.S.
It wouldn't be long until that privilege turned into a nightmare, as they say in an interview with creator, full-time RV-er, and consumer advocate Liz Amazing. You can see that interview, together with photos that back up their claims, at the bottom of the page.
Everything was good until it wasn't According to the pair, they traveled to California from their home base in Utah to take delivery of their Pebble Flow and were thrilled when the inspection revealed that everything was in order. Ryan, who describes himself as a worker in the solar industry, says the high autonomy of the Pebble Flow was what attracted him to it in the first place.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing With inspection cleared, the two hitched their Pebble and started the drive back home, and that's when the first issues began. Active Tow Assist, which is the system that helps with towing, stopped functioning on the highway, resulting in strain and drag, and causing stability issues.
The issues continued once they arrived home. They noticed one of the flexible solar panels on the roof had flown off and that the charger stopped functioning with the trailer in storage, locking the system down as the battery drained and leaving them with a techny piece of machinery they no longer had any control over.
Ryan and Celeste never got the chance to go out camping with their trailer, but they did borrow it to his brother for a couple of weeks, and other issues arose. The trailer lost a stabilizer foot on the road, the solar panels became delaminated and stopped working at maximum capacity, and worse yet, it began showing signs of structural degradation.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing Again, for a trailer they never got the chance to use for its intended purpose, the couple were shocked to see cracks appear in the fiberglass on the corners of the windows and of the door, cracks in weather seals, and the rear emergency escape window became wrapped. Issues also appeared inside, especially in the trim and finishes.
Ryan and Celeste were in contact with Pebble RV from the first signs of trouble and with the technician they sent out in the field to handle the issues. At one point, they were getting contradictory messages: the technician was telling them that the unit would be sent back to the factory for inspection and repairs, while a service manager was saying it wouldn't be, offering the owners retail gift cards instead.
In May this year, the two had had enough of the trailer and formally asked Pebble for a buyback. According to them, it took the company six weeks to finally answer their request, though they still maintained contact – and it was a refusal to take the faulty unit off their hands.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing "We're afraid to take it out – who knows what's going to fly off next... Owning this has now become a liability," Ryan says. They're not willing to consider keeping the unit, after months of issue and exactly zero use.
Liz says she tried to get a response from the Pebble management, but to no avail. We also reached out but are still waiting for a reply.
Liz's followers flooded Pebble on social media with comments and queries, and one of them finally got a reply. "We're talking to the customer and will make it right," Pebble says.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing The trailer of the future The Pebble Flow debuted in 2023 as a concept and the first Founders Edition units started going out to the first backers in the fall of 2025. Imagined as a trailer of the future, it uses tech and minimalist design to elevate the RV experience while still offering the creature comforts of home.
The trailer measures 25 feet (7.6 meters) in total length and rides on a single axle, offering a cargo carrying capacity of 1,000 lbs (453 kg) and a gross weight of 6,800 lbs (3,084 kg). It comes with two sleeping areas, one at each end and with extra functionality during the day: a U-shaped dinette and a home office, respectively.
Photo: Pebble RV The galley is on the campside, all-electric and with storage in the lower half. Across the way is the full and dry bathroom behind walls of electrochromic glass, the same glass you get all around the trailer .
Everything onboard runs off 1kW of solar on the roof and a 45kWh battery bank. The "brain" of the Pebble Flow is the Nvidia Drive Orin SoC, which offers features like InstaCamp, Magic Hitch, and Auto Dump, allowing you to perform operations (parking, hitching, or dumping the black water) on the Pebble app.
Photo: Pebble RV The travel trailer also comes with Starlink, a four-camera system, and 40 gallons (151 liters) of fresh water, 37 gallons (140 gallons) of gray, and 18 gallons (68 liters) of black water.

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.
Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.
Surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?
The bet Musk won’t let go
After Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) said there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time . In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a new video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”
What Tesla is actually selling
On Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.
As we reported Friday , the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement says it “will not operate” without the $299 plan, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.
So Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.
MKBHD: “My hair is safe”
Brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.
The memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026 My hair is safe for several reasons 1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat 2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c — Marques Brownlee (@MKBHD) November 14, 2026
Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:
He’s a chicken — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 14, 2026
Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.
But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:
“It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”
That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.
Electrek’s Take
Yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.
Tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version shows up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.
This Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.
What do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.
You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.
This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

Autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.
Greenzie announced the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.
And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet , the company really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.
“We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” says Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”

Greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial , as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.
“Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”
Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous
Image by Mean Green Products.
The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.
Mean Green claims that the combination of big battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.
The company says the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.
A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.
